about: UX choices that have more than one legitimate pattern. Each entry names an outcome the signed scope requires and the normal patterns that can meet it, where neither the contract nor the platform fixes one. An entry exists only where choosing early would constrain the design for no reason. It adds no capability: it is about how a contracted capability is presented.

statuses.open: No pattern is preferred yet. The designer proposes, recommends one and shows the alternatives.
statuses.provisional: A working baseline for the first wireframes. Not a requirement and not an owner-confirmed final product decision. It may change in UX review without a scope change, provided the pattern chosen still meets the requirement and the constraints.
statuses.locked: A pattern was selected at its decision stage, and decision_source says by whom and where.

decision_stages.low_fidelity_review: The owner's review of the low-fidelity wireframes.
decision_stages.high_fidelity_review: The owner's review of the high-fidelity design.
decision_stages.localisation_review: The design and localisation review of the Arabic experience.

options.name: Numerals in Arabic
options.requirement_outcome: Numbers, prices and dates are formatted per locale in English and in Arabic (NFR-04b).
candidate_patterns: Western digits 0 to 9 in both languages
Arabic-Indic digits in running Arabic text, Western digits for prices, quantities and reference numbers
options.working_baseline: Western digits 0 to 9 in both languages
constraints: Currency, number and date formatting follows the locale (NFR-04b, accepted by #269).
Order numbers, tracking numbers, phone numbers and codes must stay unambiguous and copyable.
Whatever is chosen is applied consistently across pages, emails and invoices.
selection_criteria: what the audience reads most easily
consistency with payment, carrier and invoice documents
options.decision_source: Owner working baseline, D-14, 6 October 2026. A starting point for the first wireframes, not a final decision.

options.name: Product-list continuation
options.requirement_outcome: A customer can continue through a product list beyond the first set of products (PLP-16) and sees how many results there are (PLP-17).
constraints: PLP-16 names pagination or infinite scroll and fixes neither.
A place in a list must have an address that can be shared, reopened and indexed (NFR-03).
The footer must stay reachable.
Usable by keyboard and screen reader (NFR-11).
options.decision_source: Owner working baseline, D-14, 6 October 2026. A starting point for the first wireframes, not a final decision.

options.name: Checkout structure
options.requirement_outcome: The customer gives an address, chooses shipping and payment, reviews the order and places it (JRN-07, CHK-01 to CHK-09), on a mobile-optimised checkout (CHK-10).
candidate_patterns: One page with progressive or accordion sections
Stepped checkout, only if it stays compatible with the contracted behaviour and the chosen commerce implementation
constraints: A review of the order comes before Place Order (CHK-05).
The WooCommerce Checkout block is the native baseline, and native comes first (constitution M-4).
Guest checkout is never forced into registration (AUTH-07).
Place Order creates exactly one order (PAY-05).
selection_criteria: clarity of the total at every point
what the native checkout supports without custom code
options.decision_source: Owner working baseline, D-14, 6 October 2026. A starting point for the first wireframes, not a final decision.

options.name: Filter placement on desktop and tablet
options.requirement_outcome: A customer narrows a list by category, brand, price, attribute and availability, and sees and removes each active filter (PLP-06 to PLP-10, PLP-18).
candidate_patterns: Horizontal filter bar above the grid
constraints: On mobile the filters are a drawer: PLP-22 names it. That part is not open.
The WooCommerce product filter blocks are the native baseline.
Search results carry the full filter set (SRCH-04), so the pattern must work there too.
selection_criteria: how many filters and options a category really has

options.name: Mini-cart presentation
options.requirement_outcome: The header shows the cart with a live item count (NAV-06) and a mini-cart (CART-12), and the customer sees that an item was added (PDP-08).
candidate_patterns: Drawer that opens after an add, with the count alone at other times
constraints: A mini-cart in the header is contracted (CART-12). It cannot be reduced to a link to the cart page.
The cart page remains (IA-08).
The WooCommerce mini-cart block is the native baseline.
selection_criteria: how much an add interrupts browsing

options.name: Keeping the buy actions in reach on the product page
options.requirement_outcome: Add to Cart and Buy Now are available on the product page (PDP-08, PDP-09).
candidate_patterns: Buy area in the page flow only
Sticky buy bar on mobile once the buy area has scrolled away
Sticky buy area beside the gallery on desktop
constraints: A variable product needs a choice before it can be added (PDP-05).
The stock state is visible wherever the action is (PDP-06, PDP-22).
A sticky element must not cover content, the consent banner or the keyboard.
selection_criteria: whether it distracts from the product

options.name: Gallery navigation and zoom
options.requirement_outcome: A customer browses a product's images and video and can zoom (PDP-01, PDP-02).
candidate_patterns: Thumbnail strip with a main image
Image grid on desktop, swipe on mobile
constraints: Zoom must exist (PDP-01). Its mechanism, hover magnifier, lightbox or pinch, is chosen with the navigation pattern.
Video sits in the same gallery (PDP-02).
Order and swipe follow the reading direction. The image is never mirrored.
The WooCommerce product gallery block is the native baseline.
selection_criteria: number of images a product really has

options.name: How the category navigation opens on desktop
options.requirement_outcome: Customers reach categories through an admin-managed mega menu or category navigation (NAV-07).
candidate_patterns: Opens on hover and on keyboard focus
constraints: The structure is managed by the client (NAV-07, SSC-07), so depth and length are not fixed.
Fully operable by keyboard (NFR-11).
The core navigation block is the native baseline.

options.name: How the mobile menu shows category levels
options.requirement_outcome: On mobile the navigation is reached from a menu button (NAV-10) and carries the same category structure (NAV-07).
candidate_patterns: Drill-down: one level per panel, with a way back
constraints: The menu also carries the language switcher and the account and wishlist entry points (NAV-02, NAV-04, NAV-05).
Opens from the mirrored edge in Arabic.

options.name: Search interaction
options.requirement_outcome: A clear, prominent search bar (NAV-03), quick search on mobile (NAV-09), and suggestions as the customer types (SRCH-03).
candidate_patterns: Inline field with a suggestions panel
Field that expands in the header
constraints: The search bar is prominent on desktop (NAV-03): it is not hidden behind an icon there.
No external search provider (SRCH-09 and INT-15 are P2). What suggestions can contain follows what #304 selects.
Works with Arabic input in both reading directions (SRCH-06a).
selection_criteria: what the suggestions can really contain

options.name: Product information layout
options.requirement_outcome: The product page carries the key features, the full description, the specifications, delivery information, the returns summary and the authenticity statement (PDP-11 to PDP-16).
candidate_patterns: Tabs on desktop, accordion on mobile
constraints: PDP-12 words the full description as a tab. Read that row in the signed register before choosing anything other than tabs on desktop.
Product content differs in length between English and Arabic (SSC-21).
selection_criteria: how much content a product really has
whether content is hidden from the customer or from search engines

options.name: Home hero: one banner or a slider
options.requirement_outcome: An admin-managed hero at the top of the home page (HOME-01).
constraints: HOME-01 names a banner or a slider and fixes neither.
What an editor can change is set by the curated section library (register section G11).
A slider is operable by keyboard and does not move against a reduced-motion preference (NFR-11).
selection_criteria: how many campaigns run at once
